ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure draws multiple molecular structures containing lone pair electrons. In the upper-left structure there is a nitrogen atom N, a pair of lone pair electrons is drawn on the nitrogen, and it is connected to three carbon groups; in the lower-right structure there is also a nitrogen atom N, lone pair electrons are drawn on the nitrogen, and it is connected to a carbon group and hydrogen. Other heteroatom structures with lone pair electrons, such as fluorine and oxygen, can also be seen in the figure. Reasoning: According to the question stem and the specified method, when all these bases act as Brønsted-Lowry bases, they accept H+ through the same atom. A Brønsted-Lowry base accepting a proton corresponds to a Lewis base providing an electron pair: H+ itself is electron-deficient and accepts the lone pair electrons from the basic atom to form a new N-H bond. The specified method indicates that the common basic site is the nitrogen atom, so protonation is completed by the hydrogen ion connecting to the lone pair electrons on the nitrogen atom.

method.method_draft: First read the diagram to locate the atom in the bases that has the available lone pair used for protonation. Then read the question statement that all bases accept a hydrogen ion to the same atom. Apply the Brønsted-Lowry/Lewis connection: accepting H+ occurs when the lone pair on that atom forms a bond to H+. Since the shared basic site indicated is nitrogen, conclude that the hydrogen ion attaches to the lone pair on the nitrogen atom.
